title: Dehumidifier for Window Condensation: Stop Foggy Windows (2026)
h1: Condensation on Your Windows? How a Dehumidifier Stops It
dek: Fogged glass isn't a window problem. It's humid indoor air meeting the coldest surface in the room, and the fix starts with the air.
description: Does a dehumidifier stop window condensation? Why windows fog, the humidity levels that trigger it by window type, and the dehumidifier setup that fixes it.
intro: Wake up to streaming glass every winter morning and it's tempting to blame the windows. In most cases, though, **window condensation** is a sign that the air inside holds more moisture than the cold glass can tolerate. The right **dehumidifier** fixes it by lowering the room's humidity until its dew point drops below the temperature of the glass, so the water stays in the air rather than beading on the pane.

The tricky part is that there's no single magic number. The humidity level that triggers condensation depends on how cold it is outside and whether your windows are single-, double- or triple-pane. That's why the same room can stay clear in October and fog solid by January.
Below, we explain what's happening, show the thresholds by window type, and walk through the setup — and the few dehumidifiers and tools — that solve it for good.

blocks.text: Warm air holds more water vapor than cold air. In winter, the inside surface of a window is usually the coldest thing in the room. When room air touches it, that air cools right at the glass. If it cools below its dew point, the excess moisture comes out as liquid. The colder it is outside, the colder the glass, and the lower your indoor humidity has to be to keep it clear.

blocks.title: The single-pane catch
blocks.text: On a 10°F night, a single-pane window can fog at just 17% humidity — well inside the EPA's normal 30–50% range. In that case, a dehumidifier helps, but storm windows or upgraded glazing may be the real fix.

We don't run a test house. We drew on published building-science calculations for condensation thresholds by glazing type, EPA humidity guidance, manufacturer specs for humidistat precision and capacity, and owner reports about winter performance.

sections.heading: Does a dehumidifier stop window condensation?

blocks.text: Yes, in most homes — as long as the moisture is indoors and on the room side of the glass. Lowering the room's humidity lowers its dew point, and once that's below the glass temperature, the fog stops forming. It won't help in three situations:

items: **Condensation between the panes.** Moisture trapped inside a double- or triple-glazed unit means the seal has failed. That's a window repair, not a humidity problem.
**Dew on the outside of the glass.** Exterior condensation on summer mornings is common with efficient windows and is harmless.
**A single-pane window in deep cold.** If the threshold is below 20%, holding the room that dry is impractical and uncomfortable. Add storm windows or interior insulating panels.

sections.heading: How to stop condensation on windows

items: **Cut moisture at the source.** Run bathroom and kitchen exhaust fans vented outdoors, cover pots, and dry laundry in a vented dryer.
**Find your threshold.** Use a hygrometer to note the room's humidity on a morning the windows fog.
**Set the dehumidifier a few points lower.** Put the unit in the room, not aimed at the glass, and close the door so it isn't drying the whole house.
**Keep air moving at the glass.** Open blinds and pull heavy drapes back a few inches; trapped, still air against the pane gets colder and fogs sooner.
**Adjust as the season changes.** Lower the setpoint before a cold snap and raise it again in spring.

blocks.text: Turning up the heat can briefly clear the glass, but it doesn't remove any moisture; the water will reappear elsewhere once the room cools. Our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) has seasonal targets, and our guide on [how to dehumidify a room](/guides/how-to-dehumidify-a-room/) covers the non-appliance fixes in detail.

blocks.text: Foggy windows are a symptom of indoor humidity meeting cold glass. Cut moisture where it starts, find your fogging threshold with a hygrometer, and set a dehumidifier like the **Midea Cube 35** a few points below it. If the condensation is between the panes, call a window pro instead. And if it's showing up all over the house, it's time to think whole-home.

faqs.q: Will a dehumidifier stop condensation on windows?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Lowering indoor humidity brings the room's dew point below the glass temperature, so moisture stops forming. It won't fix condensation between the panes of a sealed window or dew on the outside of the glass.

faqs.q: What humidity level stops window condensation?
faqs.a: It depends on the outdoor temperature and the glass. At 30°F outside, single-pane windows can fog above about 32% humidity, while double-glazed windows tolerate up to about 58%. The colder it gets, the lower the indoor humidity needs to be.

faqs.q: Is there such a thing as a window dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Not as a separate appliance that mounts in a window. Window air conditioners remove some moisture as they cool, but in winter you need a portable dehumidifier placed in the room. Small absorbent strips or trays for sills catch drips but don't lower humidity.

faqs.q: Where should I put a dehumidifier for window condensation?
faqs.a: In the room with the fogging windows, a few feet from walls and furniture, with the door closed. It doesn't need to point at the glass; lowering the whole room's humidity is what stops the fog.

It can be. Water running onto sills and frames keeps them damp, which can lead to peeling paint, rot and mold, especially when it happens every night. It's also a sign the room's humidity may be affecting other cold surfaces.

faqs.q: Why do I get condensation on double-pane windows?
faqs.a: Double glazing raises the threshold but doesn't eliminate it. A very cold night, a humid room such as a bathroom or kitchen, or a degraded seal can still push the glass below the room's dew point.
